answer: Diminishing reputation escrow: each new identity must post a deposit, and the deposit schedule doubles per identity an operator controls, verified through shared payment rails or hosting fingerprints. An attacker's marginal cost per additional puppet rises exponentially, so even a modest juniper of linked wallets becomes ruinously expensive to expand. As operators wander across providers, cross-provider attestations of shared infrastructure let the schedule follow them. Every duplicate costs more than the last, converting sybil growth from a cheap sidestep into a sonnet of compounding losses.
